case.label: E
case.text: GuardDuty S3 Protection does raise a finding when server access logging is turned off on a bucket (a Stealth-type finding from CloudTrail management events), so an EventBridge rule on that finding could turn logging back on automatically with little custom code. It fails only because a finding is triggered by the change event: buckets whose logging is already off today produce no finding, and the stem explicitly requires those buckets too. That clause decides the item cleanly. C works functionally but is custom code to run and maintain, so it loses on LEAST operational overhead; D fails because Config proactive mode evaluates resource configurations before deployment and does not block API calls on account-level settings. A minor unstated detail (Config recording and the rule must be deployed in every member account and Region, for example through a conformance pack that carries the remediation) does not change which options are best.
